name: Britney Spears
description:
'''Britney Jean Spears''' (born December 2, 1981) is an American singer. Referred to as the "[[Princess of Pop]]", she is known for her unique vocal style and energetic stage performances. Spears's role in reviving [[teen pop]] music established her as the best-selling teenage artist of all time and [[Cultural impact of Britney Spears|one of the most influential entertainers of the early 21st century]].

Spears began her career in the early 1990s as a cast member of the musical ''[[Ruthless!]]'' and the final two seasons of ''[[The All-New Mickey Mouse Club]]''. After signing with [[Jive Records]] in 1997, she released her debut single, "[[...Baby One More Time]]", which topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and became one of the [[List of best-selling singles|best-selling singles in history]]. Her first two albums, ''[[...Baby One More Time (album)|...Baby One More Time]]'' (1999) and ''[[Oops!... I Did It Again (album)|Oops!... I Did It Again]]'' (2000), are among the [[List of best-selling albums|world's best-selling albums]], while her third album, ''[[Britney (album)|Britney]]'' (2001), became a [[List of best-selling albums of the 21st century|21st-century bestseller]]. In 2002, she starred in the film ''[[Crossroads (2002 film)|Crossroads]]''. Her fourth album, ''[[In the Zone]]'' (2003), featured the single "[[Toxic (song)|Toxic]]", which won a [[Grammy Award for Best Dance Recording]].

Spears's highly publicized personal struggles influenced her fifth album, ''[[Blackout (Britney Spears album)|Blackout]]'' (2007). After her involuntary placement under a conservatorship, Spears released the albums ''[[Circus (Britney Spears album)|Circus]]'' (2008), ''[[Femme Fatale (Britney Spears album)|Femme Fatale]]'' (2011), ''[[Britney Jean]]'' (2013) and ''[[Glory (Britney Spears album)|Glory]]'' (2016). With "[[Womanizer (song)|Womanizer]]", "[[3 (Britney Spears song)|3]]", and "[[Hold It Against Me]]", she became the third woman to [[List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones#Most consecutive decades charting a number-one song|top the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 in three separate decades]]. In 2019, Spears withdrew from regular concert touring to focus on [[Britney Spears conservatorship case|her controversial conservatorship case]]. She later testified against her family and management for maltreatment, leading to the conservatorship's termination in 2021. Spears announced her departure from the music industry in 2024, and sold her music catalogue for a reported $200 million in 2026.

Spears is one of the [[best-selling music artists of all time]], with estimated sales of over 150 million records. ''[[Forbes]]'' named her as the world's [[Forbes list of the world's highest-paid musicians#Female|highest-paid female musician]] in 2000 and 2012. She was ranked among the [[Time 100|100 most influential people in the world]] by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' (2021) and the [[Billboard's Greatest Pop Stars|greatest pop stars of the 21st century]] by ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' (2023). Her [[List of awards and nominations received by Britney Spears|accolades]] include one [[Grammy Award]], six [[MTV Video Music Awards]] (including the [[Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award]]), seven [[Billboard Music Awards|''Billboard'' Music Awards]] and a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]]. Spears has launched [[Britney Spears products|numerous products]], with her 2005 fragrance [[Fantasy (fragrance)|Fantasy]] with [[Elizabeth Arden, Inc.]] generating over $1.5 billion in sales by 2011. Her life and career were the subject of the documentary ''[[Framing Britney Spears]]'' (2021) and memoir ''[[The Woman in Me (memoir)|The Woman in Me]]'' (2023).
